description: Pune regional ruleset — transcribed from Pune_menu_rulebook_101.xlsx (R1-R70). Standalone: it does NOT extend Bangalore, because most Bangalore rules describe Bangalore's rulebook (theme days, the deep-fried coupling family, the non-veg station) and Pune's rulebook states its own set. docs/pune_rulebook.md maps every R-number to the rule below that implements it, and lists the ones that are not machine-encodable.

rules._comment: General 20-day no-repeat window for any single dish; also covers the same-item side of R30/R31/R37's 15-day gaps.
rules.name: item_cooldown_20d

rules._comment: No dish twice in one horizon. Pune's whole Gaps section (R28-R38) presumes it.
rules.name: unique_items_session

rules._comment: R27 — a full week's combination must not repeat within a month.
rules.name: no_repeat_weeks

rules._comment: The Pune rulebook defines no theme days (its only mention of one is R3's 'except on Chinese day'), so this is here for cuisine hygiene, not for a rotating theme: it keeps chinese and continental mains off a day that is not their theme, and holds the gravy/veg-dry/bread to the counter's configured cuisine. `rice` is EXEMPT on purpose — Pune's rice slot is where the region lives (masala_bhat, phodnicha_bhat, and the lemon/jeera/ghee rice baths are all tagged south_indian), and narrowing a north-themed counter to the 10 north rices would both delete the Maharashtrian dishes and leave 8 of those 10 under mixedveg_pulao_biryani_weekly's cap of 1 — five rice days from two uncapped items, which is force-violated, not tight. Salads are exempt via EXEMPT_FROM_CUISINE, which matters here because every salad in the Pune list is tagged continental.
rules.name: theme_cuisine_filter

rules._comment: R1 (min 3 distinct colours/day) + R2 (max two items may look alike) + R3 (rice and gravy differ, except on a chinese day). Pune is flatter than Bangalore on both counts: 3 distinct rather than 4, and NO colour may reach 3 (max_colors_at_reach 0), because R2 states the cap without an exception.
rules.name: colour_three_distinct_max_two_alike

rules._comment: The list carries exactly TWO curd_side dishes (raita, boondi_raita), so a counter serving Curd / Raita every day must repeat them — uniqueness is already lifted for that by the arithmetic starved-slot exception. The 20-day cooldown is the part that breaks: once a week is SAVED both dishes are in history and the slot has no candidate at all, so week 2 answers 422 'cooldown banned all 2 curd side candidates'. A yogurt side is a staple accompaniment, not a variety slot — plain `curd` is already globally repeatable for the same reason (constants.REPEATABLE_SLOTS). Same fix as R36 for bread, same cause.
rules.name: raita_is_a_staple

rules._comment: R36 — plain atta phulka/chapathi may run on consecutive days. Pune's bread slot is chapati/phulka only, so they are staples like steamed rice: exempt from unique_items and from the 20-day ban. Without this the second week has both breads cooled down and no bread left.
rules.name: plain_chapati_may_repeat

rules._comment: R12 — aloo-based gravies max twice a week.
rules.name: aloo_gravy_twice_weekly

rules._comment: R14 — black chana gravies max once a week. is_black_chana_gravy was 0 for every row in the raw workbook, which made this inert; scripts/pune_flag_corrections.py sets it on black_chana_malwani.
rules.name: black_chana_gravy_weekly

rules._comment: R16 — kabuli chana gravies max once a week.
rules.name: kabuli_chana_gravy_weekly

rules._comment: R20 (mixed-veg part) — mixed-veg gravies max once a week.
rules.name: mixed_veg_gravy_weekly

rules._comment: R20 (kurma part) — veg kurma gravies max once a week.
rules.name: veg_kurma_gravy_weekly

rules._comment: R20 (kofta part) + R18 (malai kofta) + R32 (kofta needs a 7-day gap) — one kofta gravy per week covers all three inside a weekly horizon. R6 (malai kofta excludes other premium gravies that week) follows from premium_gravy_weekly below.
rules.name: veg_kofta_gravy_weekly

rules._comment: R30 — kadhi-style dal once in 15 days; projected onto the horizon as once a week (the 20-day item cooldown carries the rest of the window for the same dish). Kadhi sits under veg_gravy in the ontology.
rules.name: kadhi_weekly

rules._comment: R30's 15-day window, enforced across plans from saved history (kadhi_weekly is the within-plan half). A kadhi served last week is held off until the 15 days clear, not just kept to one per week.
rules.name: kadhi_15d_window

rules._comment: R22 — premium-ingredient gravies max once a week.
rules.name: premium_gravy_weekly

rules._comment: R23 — premium-ingredient veg dry max once a week.
rules.name: premium_veg_dry_weekly

rules._comment: R13 — at most one premium veg item on a day, counted across every slot (a paneer gravy and a soya dry on the same day is two).
rules.name: premium_veg_daily_max_1

rules._comment: R5 + annexure (Premium Ingredients: baby corn, kofta) — baby-corn dishes max once a week. In the Pune list baby corn appears in salads.
rules.name: baby_corn_weekly

rules._comment: R15 — deep-fried veg dry once per 7 days.
rules.name: deep_fried_veg_dry_weekly

rules._comment: R31 — leafy veg dry once in 15 days; projected onto the horizon as once a week. is_leafy_based_dish covered no veg dry in the raw workbook; scripts/pune_flag_corrections.py adds the palak / methi / hariyali dishes.
rules.name: leafy_veg_dry_weekly

rules._comment: R31's 15-day window across plans (leafy_veg_dry_weekly is the within-plan half): a leafy veg dry served last week is held off until the 15 days clear.
rules.name: leafy_veg_dry_15d_window

rules._comment: R43 — only one leafy-based dish per day's menu, across all slots.
rules.name: leafy_daily_max_1

rules._comment: R21 — pappu dal once a week.
rules.name: pappu_dal_weekly

rules._comment: R25 — the remaining dal days should be mostly yellow dal ('roughly one every 3 days'). Read as a floor over the horizon: at least 2 of a 5-day week. min targets auto-cap to what is placeable, so a shorter horizon or a thinner pool lowers it rather than failing.
rules.name: yellow_dal_at_least_twice

rules._comment: R19 — mixed veg pulao / biryani max once a week.
rules.name: mixedveg_pulao_biryani_weekly

rules._comment: R17 — maida-based breads max once a week. Inert in the current Pune list (no maida breads); kept as a stated rule.
rules.name: maida_bread_weekly

rules._comment: R47 — oil-based breads (lachha parota, poori) are monthly. A month is longer than any horizon, so this caps them at one per horizon; the 20-day item cooldown extends it for the same dish. Inert in the current Pune list.
rules.name: oil_based_bread_weekly

rules._comment: R47's monthly window enforced across plans from history: once an oil-based bread is served it is held off for 30 days, so the cadence is truly monthly and not once-a-week. Inert in the current Pune list (no oil-based breads).
rules.name: oil_based_bread_monthly_window

rules._comment: R34 — multigrain breads must not run on consecutive days. Inert in the current Pune list.
rules.name: multigrain_bread_non_consecutive

rules._comment: R33 — dal colour must not repeat on consecutive days.
rules.name: dal_colour_non_consecutive

rules._comment: R28 — dessert form (dry / semi-dry / wet) must not repeat on consecutive days.
rules.name: dessert_form_non_consecutive

rules._comment: R35 — north-Indian flavoured rice should not run on consecutive days. SOFT, at high priority: a counter themed north every weekday cannot satisfy a hard version (every day's rice is north by construction), and a hard rule that is provably force-violated is a config error rather than a menu constraint — so the honest encoding is a strong preference. Same for the south rule below.
rules.name: avoid_consecutive_north_rice

rules._comment: R38 — south-Indian flavoured rice should not run on consecutive days (soft, see above).
rules.name: avoid_consecutive_south_rice

rules._comment: R13 support — keep the week's premium gravy and premium veg dry on different days rather than merely capping them per day.
rules.name: premiums_different_days

rules._comment: R64/R65 support (balance and variety across the meal) — vary the gravy's key ingredient across the week instead of five paneer variants. Soft.
rules.name: veg_gravy_key_ingredient_variety

rules._comment: R64/R65 support — same for veg dry.
rules.name: veg_dry_key_ingredient_variety

rules._comment: Paneer belongs on a mix / south / north day; chinese and biryani days are the fallback, not the default (client rule, all cities). SOFT on purpose: the hard equivalent is selector_frequency.allowed_day_types, which forbids paneer on the other days outright — and a counter themed chinese or biryani every weekday would then never serve paneer at all. `holiday` (a weekend day on a serve_weekends counter) is not in the preferred list either, so paneer lands on a working day.
rules.name: paneer_prefers_mix_south_north_days

rules._comment: No soya, baby corn, chole or mushroom on a paneer day (client rule, all cities) — they read as substitutes for each other, so serving two wastes a slot. Counted across every slot because the point is the day's plate: a paneer gravy next to a soya veg dry is exactly the pairing to avoid. 'chole' is selected as the chana-gravy family (is_chana_gravy) since that is how the ontology files chole in both cities; the flag also covers the other whole-legume gravies, which fits the intent. Pune carries no mushroom dish, so that part of the selector is simply inert there. Baby corn is matched on the NAME, not on key_ingredient: that column tags 67 Bangalore rows baby_corn of which only 3 are baby-corn dishes (it is the de-facto default for a mixed salad, incl. iceberg_lettuce and black_olives) while the 34 dishes actually named after baby corn are tagged corn / bell_pepper / cauliflower. A HARD rule on that column would ban nearly every salad from paneer days and still miss 31 of the 34 real dishes. A dish matching BOTH sides (chole_paneer) counts as paneer only — see SameDayExclusionRule._hits.
rules.name: paneer_not_with_soya_babycorn_chole_mushroom
